questions.question: In Baudelaire's "The Albatross," the poet resembles the albatross because: a) a) Both are beautiful creatures b) Both are kings of their respective domains b) c) Both suffer when removed from their natural element d) Both have large wings
questions.solution_html:
• “The Albatross” - change from Romanticism to Symbolism - stands between two big poetry styles
  • - a bridge poem. Romantic aspect - Poet as Hero - loved nature and freedom - albatross is “king of
  • the sky” and “prince of the clouds” - flies high in storms and laughs at the archer (danger) - brave
  • free spirit - beautiful and majestic in the air. Symbolist aspect – hidden meaning and pain - uses
  • one image - albatross is not just a bird - Transition from dream to real world: Romanticism - poet
  • escapes to nature and imagination. - Symbolism - poet trapped in city, society, cruelty - “The
  • Albatross” shows both: Sky (Romantic) → free, high, stormy - Ship deck (Symbolist) → cruel
  • men, jokes, shame. - This change symbolises modern poetry – where art shows inner truth, not just
  • nature. Baudelaire opens the door from dreams to symbols.
questions.source_exam: REGULAR EXAMINATION NOVEMBER 2025 World Literatures in English Translation
questions.final_answer: nature. Baudelaire opens the door from dreams to symbols.

questions.question: Discuss how cultural theorists such as Raymond Williams and Stuart Hall supported polysystem approaches and contributed to rethinking translation in cultural contexts.
questions.solution_html:
• Polysystem Theory: Literature is part of a big system with high and low art. Translated books
  • fight for space in this system - Raymond Williams - Culture is ordinary daily life, not only great
  • books/works - Translators are culture makers - bring new voices - Rethinking translation - old
  • view: Translation = copy original - Williams’ view - Translation - new culture event - adds to the
  • system. Stuart Hall - Meaning is not fixed - writer codes message - reader decodes - Translator
  • decodes original culture, then recodes for new readers - Meaning changes - readers accept, change
  • or reject meaning. - Rethinking translation - Translation is not a perfect copy - negotiation between
  • cultures - Both support Polysystem - Williams: Translation joins big culture system. Hall
  • Translation changes meaning in new place.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: Translation changes meaning in new place.

• “The Albatross” - change from Romanticism to Symbolism - stands between two big poetry styles
  • - a bridge poem. Romantic aspect - Poet as Hero - loved nature and freedom - albatross is “king of
  • the sky” and “prince of the clouds” - flies high in storms and laughs at the archer (danger) - brave
  • free spirit - beautiful and majestic in the air. Symbolist aspect – hidden meaning and pain - uses
  • one image - albatross is not just a bird - Transition from dream to real world: Romanticism - poet
  • escapes to nature and imagination. - Symbolism - poet trapped in city, society, cruelty - “The
  • Albatross” shows both: Sky (Romantic) → free, high, stormy - Ship deck (Symbolist) → cruel
  • men, jokes, shame. - This change symbolises modern poetry – where art shows inner truth, not just
  • nature. Baudelaire opens the door from dreams to symbols.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: nature. Baudelaire opens the door from dreams to symbols.

questions.question: What does Natalya say to insult Ivan?
questions.solution_html:
• Natalya insults Ivan Lomov during their arguments - hurt Ivan's feelings and health - calls him bad
  • names - shows her strong temper - small fights ruin big plans. First Fight: argue over who owns
  • Oxen meadows - Second Fight: about hunting dogs - Natalya's words are funny but her insults
  • show how people fight over small things like land and pets - Ivan is weak and shy -Natalya is loud
  • and proud. Chekhov uses this to laugh at marriage and neighbours. In the end, they marry anyway
  • – love wins, but fights do not stop. /

questions.question: How does the wife’s version of events differ from the others, and what does it show about her situation?
questions.solution_html:
• Seven people tell the police what happened in the bamboo forest – Masago’s words show her
  • shame, fear, and lost honour – Woodcutter, Priest, Policeman, Mother - only see outside things – dead
  • body, rope, comb, horse - do not know the full story. Bandit Tajōmaru says he raped Masago, then
  • fought the husband with swords - won after 23 blows - Masago asked him to kill her husband and ran
  • away - Tajōmaru freed him - husband felt hate in her eyes – later someone stabbed him with a small
  • dagger while he was tied again. Masago’s Story – big differences: Tajōmaru left quickly after the
  • rape. He did not fight the husband - Husband’s eyes - she saw cold hate in his face - looked at her like
  • dirty trash – killed her husband – tried to kill herself - but is still alive, hiding in Kiyomizu Temple -
  • cannot live with shame - cannot die - trapped between life and death - takes blame - Women have no
  • voice - men speak of swords and pride - she speaks of pain, guilt, and silence - a woman crushed by
  • rules - her pain is real. /
  • x6 = 30]

questions.question: Analyze the challenges translators face in preserving meaning and cultural context? Support your answer with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Polysystem Theory: Literature is part of a big system with high and low art. Translated books
  • fight for space in this system - Raymond Williams - Culture is ordinary daily life, not only great
  • books/works - Translators are culture makers - bring new voices - Rethinking translation - old
  • view: Translation = copy original - Williams’ view - Translation - new culture event - adds to the
  • system. Stuart Hall - Meaning is not fixed - writer codes message - reader decodes - Translator
  • decodes original culture, then recodes for new readers - Meaning changes - readers accept, change
  • or reject meaning. - Rethinking translation - Translation is not a perfect copy - negotiation between
  • cultures - Both support Polysystem - Williams: Translation joins big culture system. Hall
  • Translation changes meaning in new place.
questions.source_exam: REGULAR EXAMINATION NOVEMBER 2025 World Literatures in English Translation
questions.final_answer: Translation changes meaning in new place.
